I will keep my full 30.4 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because I already know this system well, I have 30 years of experience with it, and I have well irrigation, so I can support both crops. I will not make the year complicated. For winter wheat, I will use improved seed because it is steadier than old seed and easier for me to manage on my land. I will use a medium fertilizer level, with nitrogen as the main input, plus enough phosphorus and some potassium, because wheat on my fields needs stable growth, strong tillering, and grain filling. I will irrigate about 3 times if water is normal: one for overwintering or before winter if needed, one at jointing, and one around grain filling. I will do about 2 pesticide sprays because I want to control the main diseases, aphids, and weeds without overspending. I will use rotary tillage because it fits my scale, saves labor, and works well in this rotation.

After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 30.4 mu. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because the yield is better and the stand is more uniform. I will keep fertilizer at a practical level, again with nitrogen first, because maize responds well to it, but I will still add phosphorus and potassium so the roots and ears develop better. With well irrigation, I will plan 2 irrigations, mainly around the big water-demand periods if rainfall is short. I will do about 2 pesticide applications to handle weeds and common insects, and I will continue with rotary tillage because it is the easiest and most realistic choice for me with limited family labor and some off-farm work in the household. My goal is steady yield and manageable costs, not taking risks.
